items.headline: Anthropic sets IPO price range, targets $1.4T valuation
items.summary: Anthropic will sell 825 million shares at $70 to $78 apiece, aiming to raise over $61 billion at the midpoint for a fully diluted valuation near $1.4 trillion. Trading is expected to begin November 19, making it potentially the largest IPO ever and the first pure-play frontier AI lab to go public.

items.headline: Anthropic launches Australian retail IPO amid new AI rules
items.summary: Anthropic opened its IPO to individual Australian investors as Prime Minister Albanese announced mandatory reporting for AI incidents and a new AI safety regulator with enforcement powers. Australia also ruled out a copyright exemption for training AI on local content without licensing.

items.headline: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
items.summary: Anthropic unveiled two new frontier models—Fable 5.2 for coding, reasoning and agentic tasks, and the access-restricted Mythos 5.2 for cybersecurity and life-sciences research—paired with a 20% API cost reduction. It marks the company's first frontier release since CEO Dario Amodei called to slow AI development in September.

items.headline: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon frontier model
items.summary: Google made its latest frontier model, Gemini 4 Carbon, available to developers, enterprises, scientists, and consumers, touting higher-precision knowledge work, improved agentic coding, and state-of-the-art cybersecurity. The launch intensifies the frontier model race against Anthropic and OpenAI.

items.headline: Google unveils two new specialized AI chips
items.summary: Google broadened its AI hardware portfolio with new chips including the TPU 8i Max, which combines two inference-focused TPU 8i chips to double memory, processing power, and bandwidth. The move helps hyperscalers reduce reliance on Nvidia amid growing compute demands.

items.headline: Google's November Pixel Drop adds Gemini Intelligence
items.summary: Google's November Pixel Drop brought Gemini Intelligence updates to Pixel 10 devices, along with custom widgets and the launch of Pixel Tag. The update deepens on-device AI integration across Google's hardware lineup.

items.headline: Nvidia board probes claims Huang targeted by Chinese intelligence
items.summary: Nvidia's board brought in a former federal prosecutor to investigate reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by Chinese intelligence, as shares extended their decline. Scrutiny over Huang's influence raises concerns about fallout across the broader AI ecosystem.

items.headline: METR warns Anthropic models closing in on recursive self-improvement
items.summary: METR said Anthropic's AI models are improving nearly twice as fast as before, raising AI safety alarms about recursive self-improvement. The warning follows Anthropic granting METR researchers employee-level access to independently assess its models.

items.headline: Enterprise AI spending surges 5.4x to $177 billion
items.summary: Menlo Ventures' 2026 State of Enterprise AI Report found enterprise AI spending jumped more than fivefold, from $33 billion last year to $177 billion this year, driven by the rise of AI agents. The data signals rapidly growing enterprise demand despite Wall Street skepticism about AI returns.

items.headline: Anthropic buys $3.4 billion in natural gas turbines
items.summary: Anthropic, which historically avoided physical infrastructure, is spending $3.4 billion on Caterpillar natural gas turbines capable of producing up to 1.7 gigawatts. The move underscores how AI's acute power crunch is pushing labs into energy infrastructure.

items.headline: Otter AI raises $320 million to expand into Asia
items.summary: Otter AI secured $320 million in new funding to accelerate its push into Asian markets. The raise highlights continued investor appetite for AI productivity startups despite broader market jitters.

items.headline: Oura to buy AI primary-care firm Counsel Health for $625M
items.summary: Smart-ring maker Oura agreed to acquire AI-native primary-care company Counsel Health for $625 million in cash as it weighs a public debut. The deal aims to make healthcare more proactive and personalized through responsibly designed medical AI.

items.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber for vulnerability research
items.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber, a cybersecurity model designed to find and validate software vulnerabilities. The launch reflects growing competition among AI labs to build specialized security-focused frontier models.

items.headline: Democrats plan flood of AI bills as they take Congress
items.summary: Democrats are preparing a wave of AI legislation following their midterm sweep, likely focused on safety and pre-release testing of new models. The push signals a shift toward tighter federal AI oversight despite presidential opposition.

items.headline: Cohere battles daily to secure AI computing power
items.summary: Cohere CEO Aidan Gomez said the Nvidia-backed startup faces a daily 'fight' to procure the compute it needs, pushing back on fears of overbuilding capacity. Without its own data centers, Cohere depends on cloud providers amid industry-wide compute shortages.

items.headline: Infineon raises AI chip sales forecast on data center demand
items.summary: German chip maker Infineon lifted its data center revenue guidance for fiscal 2027 to nearly 4 billion euros ($4.49 billion), up from roughly 2.5 billion euros. The upgrade signals confidence that the AI data center buildout will continue at pace.

items.headline: OpenAI introduces Images 2.6 with faster generation
items.summary: OpenAI released Images 2.6, offering faster image iteration, more control over editing rounds, GIF animation, and expanded API creation tools. The update strengthens OpenAI's creative tooling against Google and other rivals.

items.headline: Enterprises say AI regulation won't stop innovation plans
items.summary: Corporate technology leaders say they are pushing ahead with AI deployments regardless of looming regulation under Democratic control of Congress and state offices. Democrats may require pre-release testing of new AI models, but CIOs remain undeterred.

items.headline: US, China urged to stay clear-eyed on AI, Bessent says
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Bessent said the US and China should maintain a clear-eyed view on AI cooperation and competition. The remarks come amid heightened tensions over chip exports and AI leadership between the two nations.

items.headline: US AI safety division lacks permanent leader amid agent fears
items.summary: The small US government division charged with assessing the safety of new AI offerings lacks a permanent leader as public anxiety grows over reports of out-of-control AI agents. The leadership gap raises questions about federal readiness to oversee frontier AI.
